function.description: Calculate the dynamic price for a product based on the IP address of the customer while ensuring the price does not fall below a minimum floor value. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

ip_address.description: The IP address of the customer, used to determine the geographical location for pricing adjustments.

base_price.description: The base price of the product before dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

price_floor.description: The minimum allowable price for the product after dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

pricing_factor.description: A multiplier based on the customer's location, used to adjust the base price dynamically. This is a float type value.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference playbook you can use to decide *how* to price your SaaS filing service when the market looks like this:

| Competitor | One‑time filing | Annual subscription (unlimited) |
|------------|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| **A** | $99 | $149 |
| **B** | $149 | $249 |

> **Assumption:** Your product is a commodity‑style filing tool – the core value is “file a form quickly and reliably.”  
> **Goal:** Position yourself so that you capture a meaningful share of the market while still covering costs and generating profit.

---

## 1. Pick a Pricing Model

| Model | When it works | Why it matters |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| **Tiered (one‑time + subscription)** | Most common for filing services | Gives customers a clear choice between “pay‑as‑you‑go” and “all‑in‑one” |
| **Freemium + paid add‑ons** | You want to attract a large user base first | Freemium lowers acquisition cost; paid add‑ons monetize power users |
| **Usage‑based** | You have variable usage per customer | Aligns price with value delivered |
| **Hybrid** | You want both upfront and recurring revenue | Combines the best of the above |

**Recommendation:** Start with a **tiered model** (one‑time + annual). It’s the most straightforward for a filing service and matches what your competitors do.

---

## 2. Decide on Price Points

### 2.1 One‑time Filing

| Strategy | Suggested Price | Rationale |
|----------|-----------------|-----------|
| **Undercut Competitor A** | **$79** | Positions you as the cheaper “pay‑as‑you‑go” option. Good for low‑volume users. |
| **Match Competitor B** | **$149** | Keeps parity with the higher‑priced competitor; signals higher quality or extra features. |
| **Mid‑point** | **$99** | Matches Competitor A; neutral ground. |

**Why $79?**  
- **Psychological pricing**: $79 feels “cheap” but still profitable.  
- **Cost coverage**: If your cost per filing is ~$20–$30, $79 leaves a healthy margin.  
- **Competitive edge**: You’re the only one offering a lower one‑time price, which can drive trial volume.

### 2.2 Annual Subscription

| Strategy | Suggested Price | Rationale |
|----------|-----------------|-----------|
| **Undercut Competitor A** | **$129** | Gives you a $20 advantage over $149. |
| **Undercut Competitor B** | **$199** | $50 cheaper than $249. |
| **Mid‑point** | **$179** | Between $149 and $249. |

**Why $129?**  
- **Anchoring**: $129 is close to $149 but still cheaper.  
- **Value signal**: You’re offering unlimited filings for less than the “cheaper” competitor.  
- **Margin**: If your cost per filing is ~$10–$15, $129 covers many filings before hitting the break‑even point.

---

## 3. Add Value Layers

| Layer | What to Offer | How it Justifies Higher Price |
|-------|---------------|------------------------------|
| **Premium Support** | 24/7 chat, dedicated account manager | Adds perceived value for high‑volume clients |
| **Advanced Analytics** | Filing success rates, audit trails | Appeals to enterprise users |
| **API Access** | Programmatic filing | Enables integration with other tools |
| **Bulk Discounts** | 10% off for 10+ filings | Encourages larger purchases |

> **Tip:** Bundle these layers into a **“Pro” tier** that sits above the basic subscription. For example, $199/year for unlimited filings + API + priority support.

---

## 4. Pricing Psychology & Anchoring

| Technique | How to Use It |
|-----------|---------------|
| **Charm Pricing** | $99, $149, $199 – ends in 9 or 99 to feel “almost” a round number. |
| **Price Anchors** | Show a “regular” price ($149) next to a discounted price ($129) to highlight savings. |
| **Limited‑Time Offers** | “Launch special: $119 for the first 100 customers.” Creates urgency. |
| **Free Trial** | 14‑day free access to unlimited filings. Converts trial users to paying customers. |

---

## 5. Test & Iterate

| Metric | Target | How to Measure |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| **Conversion Rate** | 5–10% from free trial to paid | Funnel analytics |
| **Average Revenue Per User (ARPU)** | $120–$180 | Monthly/annual reports |
| **Churn Rate** | < 5% annually | Cohort analysis |
| **Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)** | <$50 | Marketing spend / new customers |

**A/B Testing Ideas**

| Test | Variation | Expected Insight |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| **One‑time price** | $79 vs $99 | Which drives more single‑filing revenue? |
| **Subscription price** | $129 vs $179 | Which yields higher ARPU? |
| **Bundled tier** | $199 with API vs $199 without | Does API justify the premium? |

---

## 6. Final Suggested Pricing Structure

| Tier | Features | Price |
|------|----------|-------|
| **Starter** | 1 filing per month, email support | $79 (one‑time) |
| **Basic** | Unlimited filings, email support | $129/year (or $12.99/month) |
| **Pro** | Unlimited filings, API, priority support, analytics | $199/year (or $19.99/month) |

> **Why this works:**  
> - **Starter** captures low‑budget users who only need occasional filings.  
> - **Basic** is the “value‑for‑money” tier that undercuts both competitors.  
> - **Pro** targets enterprises that need advanced features and are willing to pay a premium.

---

## 7. Quick Decision Checklist

1. **What is your cost per filing?**  
   - If <$20 → $79 is safe.  
   - If <$10 → you can push $99 or even $49 for a very aggressive strategy.

2. **Do you have differentiators?**  
   - Faster turnaround → justify $129 Basic.  
   - Better compliance checks → justify $199 Pro.

3. **What is your target market size?**  
   - Small businesses → focus on Starter + Basic.  
   - Mid‑market/enterprise → emphasize Pro tier.

4. **How fast do you need to acquire users?**  
   - Aggressive growth → launch with a $79 one‑time and $129 Basic.  
   - Steady growth → start at $99 one‑time and $149 Basic.

---

### Bottom Line

- **Set a one‑time filing price at $79** to undercut Competitor A and attract low‑volume users.  
- **Offer an annual subscription at $129** to undercut both competitors and signal better value.  
- **Add a Pro tier at $199** for advanced features and enterprise customers.  

This structure gives you a clear competitive edge, aligns with industry norms, and provides room to grow as you add features or expand into new markets. Happy pricing!
